text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE: Multiple services failing to start due to KMS signing errors (aws/gcp). Severity: SEV-2. Paging oncall -> @Samir K (primary) @Elena V (secondary). Logs attached: https://console.internal/incident/2135004321 :rotating_light:
Samir K: acked, looking now. seeing a spike in 5xxs from signing calls during startup probes.
Samir K: quick tl;dr: our service startup performs a key-sign request to cloud KMS to validate signing keys; KMS calls are timing out (504/UNAVAILABLE) which is causing startup to fail and the process to crash-retry.
Elena V: confirmed — downstream calls to both kms.googleapis.com and kms.amazonaws.com show increased p50/p95 latency and a set of 503s. metrics -> https://metrics.internal/kms/latency (graphs locked to last 30m). gRPC errors: "UNAVAILABLE" and HTTP 503.
Priya R: running smoke on staging — we can reproduce. Startup attempt 3/3 fails with: ```error: signing: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection refused``` then service exits.
Chris L: rolling restart is amplifying the problem because more instances attempt signing at once. we should stop restarts and try hotfix.
Samir K: mitigation idea 1: flip feature flag to use cached local signing key for startup (short-term only). mitigation idea 2: add aggressive exponential backoff + longer startup window to avoid immediate crash.
Priya R: on it — creating a quick feature-flag toggle in admin console. Command: `ffctl set kms_startup_fallback true --env prod`
oncall-bot: @Samir K acknowledged at 2135004350. PagerDuty incident created: PD-9876.
Samir K: performed ff toggle at 2135004420. pushing a 1-line patch to runtime to skip mandatory KMS validation on cold start when flag=true. will deploy to one region first.
Elena V: observed partial containment after toggle in us-west-2 — new instances now start, sign calls reduced ~70% because cached path used. however public traffic still shows ~12% 500s for specific request paths that attempt background key fetches.
Chris L: notif to infra: could we route KMS calls through different egress IPs/regions as a fallback? ops-bot: opened cloud support ticket with Google KMS and AWS KMS citing high-latency errors from our egress IPs. ticket ids: GCP-5421 / AWS-8342.
Priya R: customer impact summary for comms: "Some customers experienced elevated error rates (up to 12% of requests) between 21:12-21:46 UTC; root cause: third-party KMS API latency causing request signing failures and startup crashes. Mitigation: feature-flagged local signing fallback and extended startup timeouts. Full service restored for majority of customers by 21:46 UTC; residual errors observed on small subset for ~20 more minutes."
Samir K: temporary mitigation steps executed: 1) feature flag -> local-key-fallback, 2) aborted ongoing rolling restarts, 3) redeployed small canary with fallback in eu-west-1/us-west-2, 4) increased startup grace period (systemd/wrapper) to 90s, 5) enabled request-level retry with jitter for KMS calls.
Elena V: logs snippet showing KMS latency: ```[2026-03-15T21:14:02Z] KMS call to kms.googleapis.com duration=24.8s status=UNAVAILABLE```
Chris L: propagated change to autoscaler to avoid immediate new instance churn. also disabled proactive scale-up policies for 30m.
Priya R: we should inform support + customers. draft short message: "We experienced elevated latency and errors due to third-party KMS API issues impacting token signing and some API requests. Services are operational; a fallback was applied and we are monitoring. More details will follow in incident report." feedback?
Samir K: looks good. add ETA for postmortem and mitigation plan: "full postmortem within 48 hours, immediate action items listed."
oncall-bot: Handoff: @Samir K -> @Elena V for follow-through/PM. Handoff time: 2135005200.
Elena V: taking over monitoring and vendor follow-up. next steps: 1) vendor ticket updates, 2) audit all startup codepaths that synchronously call KMS, 3) add unit test to simulate KMS slow responses, 4) implement local persistent key cache with rotation policy.
Chris L: engineering action item: add circuit-breaker around KMS client (fail fast to cached key after N failures) and region-aware routing for KMS calls. also add metrics alert for sudden spike in signing-latency >=5s.
Priya R: adding an eval to Redwood Optimize that measures signing latency contribution to token request cost.
Samir K: postmortem prelim notes: probable root cause = upstream KMS control plane degradation (GCP + AWS) causing transient high latencies. contributing: synchronous startup validation, lack of robust client-side circuit breaker and no persistent key cache at boot.
Elena V: timeline notes: first errors at 21:11:43 UTC, pager at 21:12:05, feature-flag mitigation at 21:14:20, majority restored by 21:46:00, final noise cleared by 22:06:22.
Chris L: follow-on ops: request AWS/GCP to provide incident correlation IDs so we can match traces. ops-bot: ticket update posted to GCP: "We observed elevated latencies from egress IPs; please share cluster-side logs if available."
Priya R: immediate post-incident TODOs assigned in tracker: T-1212 audit startup KMS calls; T-1213 persistent signing-key cache; T-1214 client lib upgrade with circuit-breaker; T-1215 comms and customer outreach draft.
Samir K: final note — great quick coordination. next retrospective: ensure we have non-blocking startup for critical services (no external dependency must block boot).
Elena V: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated with vendor replies and will attach the incident report when ready. :white_check_mark:
